reviews.review: Good but super short 9 hrs start to finish wait for offer.
Even though this is clear anti Ork propaganda, this is still a very fun game.

Impressions and observations (spoilers, duh):
- The very start has the appropriate amount of hype and desperation that should justify a spacemarine intervention. "Delay unacceptable. Deploying the ultramarines..."
- As if on cue: "Is that wise captain? The codex astartes does not support this action..."
- Forgeworld Manufactorum announcer straight outta 1984/2024: "Be not concerned with events beyond these walls; work, focus, increase your productivity and gain the favour of the machine gods!"
- Lieutenant Mira seems like such a badass. Why don't we get a bit more of her story, and how she survived an invasion of a million orks with only a few hundred men?
- I really, really dislike the glory-kill-to-heal mechanic, especially when it's the only way and you can be damaged (and killed) during the locked-out, fairly lengthy execution animations.
- Flying around with the thunder hammer was the best part of the game. It reduces the process of killing most enemies to a mere triviality, but that seems appropriate for the `adeptus astartes'. It is wicked fun.
- Much of the combat is also entertaining and rather dynamic thanks to how easily and fluidly the game allows you to switch between melee and ranged weaponry, but I suspect the campaign will not be especially replayable. On normal difficulty, I died for the first time in chapter 7 or so, and only because I got distracted by my phone. Thereafter, I died more regularly, mostly out of impatience, though there are some annoying spots. Psykers are the worst.
- On the flip side, the boss fights in this game (and there are not too many of them), are rather lacking. Indeed the quicktime event-like feel of the final boss really takes the wind out of the game's sails, at exactly the moment when your engagement should be greatest.
- Despite everything, I didn't hate Leandros. Yeah he's a bit of a snake, but his questions make sense in this universe, and we're never given a proper answer here, despite Titus' heroic actions. The writers seem to think of him as a rule-following-rod-up-his-arse-type instead, which is quite weird for a character they keep around for almost the entire game.
- I think the macguffin in this game is quite strange. The main antagonist seems to think it's important and the guy who created is sure impressed by its warp energies, but isn't that where the chaos spacemarines are coming from anyway? Why would they "need" this particular thing to grow stronger given that they inhabit the Warp, themselves?
- Minor lore thing: the CSM enemies constantly shout something about the 'False Emperor'. Not sure if they invented it for this game, or if it connects to something, but I'm quite interested in the thinking behind that.
